strings.gui.help:
HexCleaner — Windows junk and cache cleaner.

Usage:
  {exe}
      open the program window
  {exe} {scheduled} <command> [options]
      run a command without the window, as scheduled cleanups do.
      The commands and options are the same as on the command line:
      {exe} {scheduled} help
  {exe} {disk} <folder>
      open the window on the “Disk space” tab with this folder or drive
      (this is how the Explorer context menu item starts the program)
  {exe} --help
      this help
strings.gui.error.missing_path: {option} needs a folder or drive path.
strings.cli.help:
HexCleaner — Windows junk and cache cleaner, command line.

Usage:
  {exe} analyze [what] [options]   analysis: how much junk is found; deletes nothing
  {exe} clean   [what] [options]   cleanup
  {exe} list                       items and presets
  {exe} config [action]            program settings (see below)
  {exe} trash [action]             the HexCleaner trash (see below)
  {exe} help                       this help

What to process (everything listed is combined):
  --preset <name>       preset: safe, recommended, full or the name of your own preset
                        (in quotes if it contains spaces)
  --tasks <id,id,...>   items by the ids shown by "{exe} list"
  --exclude <id,id,...> remove items from the selection
  --selected            items checked in the program window
  If nothing is specified, the items checked in the program window are used.

Options:
  --details             show the folders where junk was found
  --quiet               print only the totals
  --lang <code>         language of the output and the log, e.g. ru
  --compress-logs, --no-compress-logs
                        whether to compress logs of previous cleanups (default: as in the program)
  --close-apps          before cleaning, gracefully close programs that keep files open
                        (browsers, Steam); with analyze, only list them
  --restart-apps        start the closed programs again after the cleanup
  --no-trash            delete right away, bypassing the trash (like cleaning with Shift in the window)

Items that need administrator rights are skipped without them.
Ctrl+C stops gracefully: services are started again and the log is completed.

Files deleted by a cleanup go to the HexCleaner trash if it is enabled:
  {exe} trash                              cleanups in the trash, newest first
  {exe} trash show <cleanup> [--files]     items of a cleanup (with --files, their files too)
  {exe} trash restore <cleanup> [options]  put files back; without options, the whole cleanup
      --tasks <id,...>  only these items (ids: "trash show")
      --path <path>     only files from this folder, or this file; can be given several times
  {exe} trash delete <cleanup> --yes       delete a cleanup from the trash permanently
  {exe} trash empty --yes                  delete everything in the trash
  <cleanup> is a number from the list (1 is the newest), latest or a name like 2026-10-29 10-56-42.

Settings — the same as on the "Settings" tab of the window:
  {exe} config                       all settings with explanations and allowed values
  {exe} config get <key>             one value
  {exe} config set <key> <value>     change
  {exe} config reset <key> ...       restore the default
The window reads settings when it starts: if it is open, restart it,
otherwise it will write its own settings over yours the next time it saves.

Examples:
  {exe} analyze --preset recommended --details
  {exe} clean --preset safe --tasks recycle_bin
  {exe} clean --preset full --exclude recycle_bin,system_logs --quiet
  {exe} clean --preset "Weekly"
  {exe} clean --preset safe --no-trash
  {exe} config set trash.limit 10GB
  {exe} config set trash.policy.browsers_cache never
  {exe} trash restore latest --tasks browsers_cache

Exit codes:
  0 — done without errors
  1 — invalid arguments
  2 — done, but some files could not be deleted or some items were skipped
  3 — could not start (e.g. could not create the log)
  4 — stopped with Ctrl+C

strings.schedule.task_description: HexCleaner scheduled cleanup. Created and managed by HexCleaner.
strings.task.memory.title: Free RAM used by background processes
strings.task.memory.description: Asks Windows to page out unused memory of all processes (EmptyWorkingSet). No process is terminated.
strings.task.games_gpu_cache.title: Clean game, Steam, Epic Games and NVIDIA, AMD, Intel GPU caches
strings.task.games_gpu_cache.description: DirectX / OpenGL / Vulkan shader caches, launcher web caches and logs. Games and saves are not touched. Shader caches are rebuilt the next time you play.
strings.task.installers_cache.title: Clean NVIDIA (Installer2) and Microsoft Office (MSOCache) installer caches
strings.task.installers_cache.description: Unpacked old NVIDIA driver packages and the local copy of the Office installer. Repairing Office may then require the installation media.
strings.task.browsers_cache.title: Clean Chrome, Edge, Opera, Firefox, Yandex and other browser caches
strings.task.browsers_cache.description: Page, script and shader caches only. Cookies, history, passwords, bookmarks and extensions are not touched. Close the browsers for a complete cleanup.
strings.task.explorer_cache.title: Clean Explorer thumbnail and icon caches
strings.task.explorer_cache.description: Picture and video thumbnails, icon cache. Windows recreates them as needed. Files kept open by Explorer are skipped.
strings.task.defender_cache.title: Clean Windows Defender scan history and logs
strings.task.defender_cache.description: Scan history and Defender service logs. Quarantine and signature databases are not touched. With Tamper Protection on, some files are skipped.
strings.task.windows_setup_cache.title: Clean Windows setup cache
strings.task.windows_setup_cache.description: Windows Installer patch cache and leftovers of downloads for upgrading to a new Windows version.
strings.task.windows_update_cache.title: Clean Windows Update cache
strings.task.windows_update_cache.description: Downloaded Windows Update packages and the Delivery Optimization cache. Update services are stopped during the cleanup.
strings.task.system_logs.title: Clear Windows system logs
strings.task.system_logs.description: Windows event logs and text logs of system setup and servicing.
strings.task.driver_leftovers.title: Remove NVIDIA / AMD / Intel installer leftovers
strings.task.driver_leftovers.description: The C:\NVIDIA and C:\AMD folders where driver installers unpack themselves, and the C:\Intel\Logs logs. Installed drivers are not touched.
strings.task.user_temp.title: Delete user temporary files
strings.task.user_temp.description: The %TEMP% folder. Files younger than one hour and files in use are skipped.
strings.task.system_temp.title: Delete Windows temporary files
strings.task.system_temp.description: Temporary folders of Windows and system services. Files younger than one hour and files in use are skipped.
strings.task.diagnostics.title: Delete Windows diagnostic files
strings.task.diagnostics.description: Diagnostic and telemetry traces (ETL), power usage reports.
strings.task.user_reports.title: Delete program error reports and crash dumps
strings.task.user_reports.description: Windows Error Reporting reports and crash dumps of the current user's programs.
strings.task.recycle_bin.title: Empty the Recycle Bin
strings.task.recycle_bin.description: Permanently deletes the files in the Recycle Bin on all drives. They cannot be restored afterwards, so check the Recycle Bin first.
strings.task.system_reports.title: Delete system error reports and memory dumps
strings.task.system_reports.description: System Windows Error Reporting reports, minidumps and the full memory dump after a BSOD.
